title: Polymorphic Endpoint Surface PRD — Cohesive Behavior & Launch Playbook for Chat/Completion/Embeddings/Rerank
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: This PRD defines a single, polymorphic hosted endpoint surface that can serve chat, text completion, embeddings, and rerank workloads with unified behavioral contracts, deterministic fallback behavior, and a prescriptive launch checklist. The goal is to reduce client integration complexity while preserving per-lane performance and quality guarantees.
background: Multiple independent hosted lanes have drifted in behavior and telemetry. Clients repeatedly request a single integration that can switch lane behavior via a surface-level selector while preserving guarantees for latency, cost, and quality. Previous PRDs focused on individual lanes; this work consolidates behavioral contracts and rollout plans.
goals: Define a single endpoint contract that supports lane selector semantics for chat, completion, embeddings, and rerank
Specify per-lane acceptance criteria (latency, quality, cost) and cross-lane fallback policies
Provide an operational launch checklist (canary, telemetry, rollback) and QA matrix
Ensure backward compatibility for existing hosted clients and SDKs via adapter behavior
success_metrics: Client integration time reduced by 40% within 6 weeks post-launch (measured by developer survey and onboarding logs)
No customer-visible regression in generation quality (automated evals within 95% of baseline per-lane MRR/ROUGE/embedding-similarity)
Production p95 latency meets targets for each lane in 99% of requests during steady-state
No major incidents attributable to surface change in first 30 days
non_goals: Implementing a new stateful session migration system — out of scope for this phase
Major model architecture changes (will rely on existing model variants and quantization profiles)
Reworking Dedicated or Private deployment controls — initial rollout is Hosted-only
scope: Support selector semantics: {lane: 'chat' | 'completion' | 'embedding' | 'rerank'}. Provide typed schema for structured output, function calls for chat, embedding vectors normalization, rerank score contract, and backward-compatible defaults for clients that do not send a lane selector.
scope_changes: Initial draft required a multiplexed request body for multiple lanes in one call; changed to single-lane-per-request to simplify runtime routing and to avoid multi-tenant KV cache complexity. This reduced implementation complexity but requires clients to send parallel requests when combining lanes.
user_stories: As an SDK user, I want a single createRequest call that accepts lane selector so I don’t have to integrate four different endpoints
As an SRE, I need clear per-lane SLIs so I can write SLOs and alerting for polymorphic traffic
As a Platform PM, I want acceptance tests that cover fallback from high-cost lane variants to low-cost variants with no more than 10% quality degradation
As a Privacy Officer, I require that embedding vectors be redacted in logs and that KMS keys are used for any persisted artifacts
acceptance_criteria: API contract: POST /v1/polymorph accepts lane selector and validates against OpenAPI schema v1.0
Compatibility: Existing chat/completion/embeddings/rerank endpoints continue working for 6 months (deprecated with migration guide)
Latency targets: chat p50 < 120ms p95 < 300ms for <=2048 tokens; completion p50 < 90ms p95 < 260ms for <=1024 tokens; embeddings p50 < 40ms p95 < 120ms; rerank p50 < 150ms p95 < 420ms

Quality baselines: automated eval suites must show no >5% relative degradation on lane-specific metrics (MRR for rerank, embedding cosine recall, ROUGE/BLEU for completion) using established test prompts
Determinism & system message handling: chat system messages must be enforced by server with immutability flag; function-calling schema enforced and validated by JSON schema checks
Fallback policy: when a requested model variant is unavailable, system must fall back to declared low-cost variant with annotated response explaining fallback (X-Fallback-Model header)
Security: keys used for any persisted request/response artifacts are customer KMS-backed in hosted mode where customer has opted in
SDKs: official node/python SDKs provide adapter that maps old endpoint calls to polymorph surface with no behavior change for existing usage patterns
Telemetry: tokens/cost breakdown emitted per-request and tagged with lane and model_variant for billing and SLOs
Operational readiness: runbook and rollback plan reviewed and signed off by SRE and SOC
launch_checklist: Feature flag gate created: rollout.polymorph_endpoint.enabled (default false)
OpenAPI spec published and SDK generation pipeline updated
Conformance suite (unit + integration) passes in CI for both adapters and runtime
Canary cohort defined: 2% traffic from internal orgs, then 10%, then 25%
Canary metrics dashboard template created and shared (latency, errors, fallback rate, quality regression)
Security review completed and SOC sign-off recorded
Privacy checklist: embedding logging disabled by default, PII detection in prompt heuristics enabled
Docs & migration guide published with examples for each lane and adapter snippets
Customer communication plan drafted for deprecation window of legacy endpoints
Chaos/latency injection run against canary to validate graceful degradation and fallback behavior
Load test up to 120% expected peak QPS for each lane variant; results analyzed and annotated
Final go/no-go reviewed by Release Committee with SRE/PM/Design/Eng present
rollout_plan: Stage 0: Internal alpha (feature flag on) with evangelist teams — 1 week
Stage 1: Canary 2% external non-critical traffic for 72 hours; observe metrics and automated evals
Stage 2: Canary expansion to 10% for 7 days with targeted load tests and chaos runs
Stage 3: Gradual expansion to 25% then 50% with monitoring windows and rollback gates
Stage 4: Full rollout after 30d of stable metrics; initiate legacy endpoint deprecation timetable
smoke_tests: Basic invocation tests for each lane verifying correct response schema
Function calling flow for chat with schema-validated payloads
Embedding vector length/normalization checks and sample similarity queries
Rerank sample set producing score monotonicity and MRR sanity checks
Fallback header injection validation (X-Fallback-Model present when fallback occurs)
perf_targets: CPU/GPU utilization thresholds per model variant under target QPS
KV cache hit-rate target: >60% for chat prefix caching on conversational workload
Batching efficiency: achieve >1.6x tokens/sec improvement over naive single-request baseline in steady-state
Cold-start p95 overhead budget: <20ms for warmed GPUs, <200ms for cold containers (measured separately)
telemetry_and_alerting: Per-request tags: lane, model_variant, feature_flag_state, customer_tier
Alert: fallback_rate > 2% sustained for 10 minutes triggers P1 investigation
Alert: quality-regression-detected via automated eval (>5% drop) triggers hold on rollout
Cost telemetry: per-request token breakdown emitted to billing pipeline and daily cost-summaries per-customer
Tracing: end-to-end trace ID passed to Console for per-request debugging
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Quality regression during model variant fallback — Mitigation: conservative fallback policy + canary on internal traffic
Risk: Client confusion from single surface semantics — Mitigation: SDK adapters and migration docs with examples
Risk: Telemetry gaps during rollout — Mitigation: telemetry smoke-tests and synthetic traffic with golden responses
Risk: Increased attack surface for structured outputs — Mitigation: stricter JSON schema validation and rate limiting
decisions: Decision: single-lane-per-request retained to avoid multi-lane batching/KV cache complexity
Decision: explicit X-Fallback-Model header and response.meta.fallback_reason to keep clients informed
Decision: embeddings will be L2-normalized at the server by default with opt-out flag
Decision: structured output schema v1 enforced for function-calling and rerank payloads
open_questions: Q: Should we expose a 'priority' hint to influence scheduling for low-latency customers? (impact: routing complexity)
Q: How long should our legacy endpoints remain available before deprecation? (proposed: 6 months)
Q: Are there additional compliance controls required for EU customers around embeddings storage?
